documents.title: The four CPF accounts and what each is for
documents.summary: Your CPF savings sit in separate accounts, each with its own job. Money in these accounts earns interest and is used for housing, healthcare and retirement.
keyFacts: Ordinary Account (OA): used mainly for housing, insurance, investment and education.
Special Account (SA): a retirement-focused account for members below 55.
MediSave Account (MA): used for hospital bills and approved health insurance like MediShield Life and CareShield Life.
Retirement Account (RA): created automatically at age 55 to fund your monthly CPF LIFE payouts.

documents.title: What happens to your CPF at age 55
documents.summary: When you turn 55, CPF creates a Retirement Account for you. Savings from your Special Account, then your Ordinary Account, move into it up to your retirement sum.
keyFacts: A Retirement Account (RA) is created for you at age 55.
From 2025, the Special Account is closed at 55 and its savings move to the RA (the rest goes to the OA).
The RA holds your retirement sum, which is used to provide lifelong CPF LIFE payouts.
You can withdraw some CPF savings from age 55 (see withdrawal rules).

documents.title: How much you and your employer contribute (from 1 Jan 2026)
documents.summary: Each month, you and your employer put a share of your wages into CPF. The total rate is highest for younger workers and steps down as you get older.
keyFacts: Aged 55 and below: 37% of wages total (17% employer + 20% employee).
Rates step down for older workers; above age 70 the total is 12.5% (7.5% employer + 5% employee).
From 2026, senior worker (55-65) contribution rates rose again as part of a planned increase.
CPF contributions are payable on monthly wages above $750 (with partial rates between $50 and $750).

documents.title: The monthly salary ceiling for CPF (from 1 Jan 2026)
documents.summary: CPF contributions only apply up to a monthly wage limit, called the Ordinary Wage ceiling. This limit has been raised in steps.
keyFacts: From 1 January 2026 the CPF monthly salary (Ordinary Wage) ceiling is $8,000 — the final step of the planned increase.
Wages above the ceiling do not attract compulsory CPF contributions.
The ceiling rose in steps: $6,300 (2023) to $8,000 (2026).

documents.title: How much interest your CPF savings earn (2026)
documents.summary: CPF savings earn interest set by the government, with guaranteed floor rates. Your savings keep growing safely even when you do nothing.
keyFacts: Ordinary Account (OA): 2.5% per year (the floor rate), for 1 January to 31 March 2026.
Special, MediSave and Retirement Accounts (SMRA): 4.0% per year (the floor rate), extended until 31 December 2026.
The SMRA rate is pegged to the 12-month average yield of 10-year Singapore Government Securities plus 1%.
Interest is risk-free and backed by the Singapore Government.

documents.title: Extra interest on your first savings
documents.summary: CPF pays extra interest on your first savings so smaller balances grow faster. Seniors get even more.
keyFacts: You earn up to 5% per year if you are below age 55, and up to 6% per year if you are 55 and older.
Extra 1% is paid on the first $60,000 of your combined balances (up to $20,000 from the OA).
Members aged 55 and above earn an additional 1% on the first $30,000, on top of the above.

documents.title: Topping up your retirement and MediSave savings
documents.summary: You can voluntarily top up your own or a loved one's CPF to grow retirement savings and possibly receive tax relief.
keyFacts: The Retirement Sum Topping-Up scheme lets you top up the SA (below 55) or RA (55 and above).
You can also top up your MediSave Account for healthcare needs.
Cash top-ups may qualify for tax relief, subject to limits.
Top-ups grow at CPF interest rates and cannot be withdrawn early.

documents.title: Government matches top-ups for eligible seniors
documents.summary: For eligible lower-income seniors, the government matches cash top-ups to retirement savings dollar-for-dollar.
keyFacts: Dollar-for-dollar matching on retirement top-ups, up to $2,000 each year.
There is a lifetime matching cap of $20,000.
Aimed at seniors who have not yet reached the Basic Retirement Sum.

documents.title: Matching grant for MediSave
documents.summary: Eligible members can receive government matching on cash top-ups to their MediSave Account.
keyFacts: Dollar-for-dollar matching on MediSave top-ups, up to $1,000 a year for eligible members.

documents.title: Investing your CPF savings
documents.summary: You may invest part of your OA and SA savings through the CPF Investment Scheme if you want to seek higher returns, accepting some risk.
keyFacts: The CPF Investment Scheme (CPFIS) lets you invest OA and SA savings in approved products.
Investing carries risk; the guaranteed CPF interest is given up on invested amounts.
Suitable mainly for members comfortable with investment risk.

documents.title: Basic, Full and Enhanced Retirement Sums (2026)
documents.summary: Your retirement sum is the amount set aside at 55 to give you monthly payouts for life. There are three levels — you can aim for the one that fits your needs.
keyFacts: Basic Retirement Sum (BRS): about $110,200 for those turning 55 in 2026 (excludes rental costs; can be met partly with a property pledge).
Full Retirement Sum (FRS): about $220,400 — double the BRS.
Enhanced Retirement Sum (ERS): about $440,800 — four times the BRS — for those who want higher payouts.
Higher retirement sums give higher lifelong monthly payouts.

documents.title: CPF LIFE: monthly payouts for as long as you live
documents.summary: CPF LIFE is a national longevity insurance scheme. It gives you a monthly payout for the rest of your life, starting from age 65.
keyFacts: Payouts start at age 65 (you can defer to age 70 for higher payouts).
Standard Plan illustrative payouts: about $950/month (Basic Retirement Sum), $1,780/month (Full Retirement Sum), $3,440/month (Enhanced Retirement Sum).
Your payout depends on your Retirement Account balance when payouts begin.
Payouts continue for life, even after your CPF savings are used up.

documents.title: The three CPF LIFE plans
documents.summary: CPF LIFE offers three plans so you can choose how your payouts are shaped over time.
keyFacts: Standard Plan: higher, level monthly payouts (most members).
Basic Plan: lower monthly payouts but typically leaves more as a bequest.
Escalating Plan: payouts start lower and rise about 2% each year to help with rising prices.

documents.title: When your monthly payouts start
documents.summary: Your CPF monthly payouts begin at the payout eligibility age, which is 65. You may choose to start later for higher payouts.
keyFacts: Payout eligibility age is 65.
Deferring the start of payouts (up to age 70) increases your monthly amount.
You will be notified before you reach 65 to choose your CPF LIFE plan.

documents.title: Withdrawing CPF savings from age 55
documents.summary: From age 55 you can withdraw some CPF savings as cash, while the rest stays to provide your monthly payouts.
keyFacts: You can withdraw up to $5,000 from age 55 regardless of how much you have.
If you have more than your Full Retirement Sum, you may withdraw the balance above it (subject to rules).
Property owners can choose to set aside the Basic Retirement Sum and withdraw more, using a property pledge.

documents.title: Silver Support Scheme for seniors
documents.summary: The Silver Support Scheme gives extra quarterly cash to eligible seniors who had lower incomes during their working years.
keyFacts: Automatic quarterly payouts for eligible seniors aged 65 and above.
No application needed — eligibility is assessed automatically.
Targeted at the bottom group of seniors by lifetime wages and housing type.

documents.title: Using your CPF Ordinary Account to buy a home
documents.summary: You can use your Ordinary Account savings to help buy a home and pay the monthly housing loan, within limits.
keyFacts: OA savings can pay for the flat purchase, stamp duties and monthly mortgage instalments.
There are limits on how much OA you can use for a property.
Using more OA for housing means less left for retirement, so balance cash and CPF.

documents.title: Refunding CPF with accrued interest when you sell
documents.summary: When you sell a home bought with CPF, you must return the CPF you used plus the interest it would have earned. This protects your retirement savings.
keyFacts: When you sell, you refund the OA amount used plus accrued interest back into your CPF.
Accrued interest is the interest your used OA savings would have earned if left in CPF (2.5% per year).
If your home is pledged for retirement adequacy, the pledged amount must also be refunded on sale.

documents.title: Home Protection Scheme (HPS)
documents.summary: HPS is a mortgage-reducing insurance that protects your HDB flat if you die, become terminally ill, or are permanently disabled.
keyFacts: HPS is mandatory if you use CPF to pay your HDB monthly instalments.
It pays off or reduces the outstanding HDB loan so your family keeps the home.
Premiums can be paid from your Ordinary Account.

documents.title: Voluntarily refunding CPF used for housing
documents.summary: You can choose to return CPF savings you used for your home, even without selling, so the money earns retirement interest again.
keyFacts: A voluntary housing refund returns used OA amounts (and accrued interest) to your CPF.
The refunded savings then earn CPF interest for your retirement.
This is optional and can be done while you still own the home.

documents.title: MediSave: your healthcare savings
documents.summary: MediSave is the part of CPF set aside for healthcare. You can use it for yourself and your family for hospital stays, some treatments, and health insurance premiums.
keyFacts: MediSave pays for hospitalisation, day surgery, some outpatient treatments, and approved insurance premiums.
It can be used for approved family members too.
MediSave Care allows withdrawals of up to $200 per month for severe disability/long-term care.
There are withdrawal limits for different treatments to keep savings for future needs.

documents.title: Basic Healthcare Sum (BHS) for 2026
documents.summary: The Basic Healthcare Sum is the target amount of MediSave you aim to set aside for healthcare in old age. It is reviewed each year.
keyFacts: For members below 65, the BHS is $79,000 in 2026 (raised from $75,500 in 2025).
For members who turn 65 in 2026, the BHS is fixed at $79,000 for the rest of their lives.
MediSave savings above the BHS flow to your other CPF accounts (or are paid out at 65).

documents.title: MediShield Life
documents.summary: MediShield Life is a basic health insurance that helps pay large hospital bills and costly treatments, for life.
keyFacts: Covers large hospital bills and selected costly outpatient treatments such as dialysis.
Covers all Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents for life, including those with pre-existing conditions.
Premiums can be paid using MediSave.

documents.title: CareShield Life
documents.summary: CareShield Life is long-term care insurance that gives monthly cash payouts if you become severely disabled and need help with daily living.
keyFacts: Provides monthly cash payouts for life if you become severely disabled.
Payouts can be used for any care needs, paid in cash to you.
Premiums can be paid using MediSave.

documents.title: ElderShield
documents.summary: ElderShield is the earlier long-term care insurance scheme that pays a monthly cash payout for a limited period if you are severely disabled.
keyFacts: Pays monthly cash payouts of up to $400 for up to six years.
Being progressively replaced by CareShield Life for younger cohorts.

documents.title: MediFund: the healthcare safety net
documents.summary: MediFund is a government endowment fund that helps needy Singaporeans who still cannot afford their bills after using MediShield Life and MediSave.
keyFacts: A safety net for those who cannot pay even after other help.
Applied for through the medical social worker at the hospital or institution.
Help is assessed based on the patient's financial situation.

documents.title: CPF Nomination: deciding who receives your CPF
documents.summary: A CPF nomination lets you decide who receives your CPF savings when you pass away, and how much each person gets.
keyFacts: Without a nomination, your CPF savings are distributed by the Public Trustee under intestacy laws (which takes time and a fee).
With a nomination, savings go directly to the people you choose.
You can make or update a nomination online or at a CPF Service Centre.

documents.title: Dependants' Protection Scheme (DPS)
documents.summary: DPS is a term life insurance that pays your family a lump sum if you die, become terminally ill, or are totally permanently disabled.
keyFacts: Provides financial support to your family in difficult times.
Premiums can be paid from your CPF savings.
Covers members up to a set age.

documents.title: Closing a CPF account
documents.summary: CPF savings are paid out when you pass away (to nominees) or when you permanently leave Singapore and West Malaysia.
keyFacts: On death, savings go to nominees if you nominated; otherwise the Public Trustee distributes them.
Members permanently leaving Singapore and West Malaysia may close their accounts and withdraw all savings.
Proof of intention to leave permanently is required for closure.

documents.title: Keeping your CPF safe from scams
documents.summary: CPF offers safeguards to protect your account from unauthorised access and scams. Never share your Singpass password or one-time passwords.
keyFacts: CPF will never ask for your Singpass password or banking OTP.
The Trusted Contacts feature lets a designated person help protect your account if you are vulnerable to scams.
You can lock your CPF savings from online withdrawals for extra protection.
Always type gov.sg website addresses yourself instead of clicking links in messages.

documents.title: Viewing balances and updating your contact details
documents.summary: You can view your latest CPF balances and statements, and keep your contact details up to date, through the member portal using Singpass.
keyFacts: Log in with Singpass to view your account balances and statements.
Keep your mobile number and email current to receive CPF updates and alerts.
Updating contact preferences helps you get timely reminders.

terminology.plainEnglish: Savings used mainly for housing, insurance, investment and education.
terminology.zh: 普通账户：主要用于买房、保险、投资和教育的储蓄。
terminology.ms: Akaun Biasa: simpanan terutama untuk perumahan, insurans, pelaburan dan pendidikan.
terminology.ta: சாதாரண கணக்கு: வீடு, காப்பீடு, முதலீடு, கல்விக்கு பயன்படுத்தப்படும் சேமிப்பு.

terminology.plainEnglish: A retirement-focused savings account for members below 55.
terminology.zh: 特别账户：为55岁以下会员设立、专注退休的储蓄账户。
terminology.ms: Akaun Khas: akaun simpanan tumpuan persaraan untuk ahli di bawah 55 tahun.
terminology.ta: சிறப்பு கணக்கு: 55 வயதுக்குக் கீழ் உள்ளவர்களுக்கான ஓய்வூதிய சேமிப்பு கணக்கு.

terminology.plainEnglish: CPF savings set aside for healthcare and approved health insurance.
terminology.zh: 保健储蓄账户：预留用于医疗和批准的健康保险的公积金储蓄。
terminology.ms: Akaun MediSave: simpanan CPF untuk penjagaan kesihatan dan insurans kesihatan yang diluluskan.
terminology.ta: மெடிசேவ் கணக்கு: சுகாதாரம் மற்றும் அங்கீகரிக்கப்பட்ட காப்பீட்டுக்கான சேமிப்பு.

terminology.plainEnglish: Created at age 55 to hold your retirement sum and pay your monthly CPF LIFE payouts.
terminology.zh: 退休账户：55岁时设立，用于存放退休存款并支付每月CPF LIFE入息。
terminology.ms: Akaun Persaraan: dibuka pada umur 55 untuk menyimpan jumlah persaraan dan membayar pencen CPF LIFE bulanan.
terminology.ta: ஓய்வூதிய கணக்கு: 55 வயதில் உருவாக்கப்பட்டு மாதாந்திர CPF LIFE கொடுப்பனவை வழங்குகிறது.

terminology.plainEnglish: A national scheme that pays you a monthly amount for as long as you live, from age 65.
terminology.zh: CPF LIFE：全国终身入息计划，从65岁起每月发放，直到终老。
terminology.ms: CPF LIFE: skim kebangsaan yang membayar pencen bulanan seumur hidup, bermula umur 65.
terminology.ta: CPF LIFE: 65 வயதிலிருந்து வாழ்நாள் முழுவதும் மாதாந்திர கொடுப்பனவு வழங்கும் தேசிய திட்டம்.

terminology.plainEnglish: The lowest retirement sum target, giving basic monthly payouts; can be met partly with a property pledge.
terminology.zh: 基本退休存款：最低的退休存款目标，提供基本每月入息；可用房产抵押部分满足。
terminology.ms: Jumlah Persaraan Asas: sasaran terendah yang memberi pencen bulanan asas.
terminology.ta: அடிப்படை ஓய்வூதிய தொகை: அடிப்படை மாதாந்திர கொடுப்பனவை வழங்கும் குறைந்தபட்ச இலக்கு.

terminology.plainEnglish: Double the Basic Retirement Sum, giving higher monthly payouts for life.
terminology.zh: 全额退休存款：基本退休存款的两倍，提供更高的终身每月入息。
terminology.ms: Jumlah Persaraan Penuh: dua kali Jumlah Persaraan Asas, pencen bulanan lebih tinggi.
terminology.ta: முழு ஓய்வூதிய தொகை: அடிப்படை தொகையின் இரட்டிப்பு, அதிக மாதாந்திர கொடுப்பனவு.

terminology.plainEnglish: Four times the Basic Retirement Sum, for those who want the highest CPF LIFE payouts.
terminology.zh: 增额退休存款：基本退休存款的四倍，适合想要最高入息者。
terminology.ms: Jumlah Persaraan Dipertingkat: empat kali Jumlah Persaraan Asas untuk pencen tertinggi.
terminology.ta: மேம்படுத்தப்பட்ட ஓய்வூதிய தொகை: அடிப்படை தொகையின் நான்கு மடங்கு, அதிக கொடுப்பனவுக்கு.

terminology.plainEnglish: The target amount of MediSave to set aside for healthcare in old age; $79,000 in 2026.
terminology.zh: 基本保健存款：为年老医疗预留的保健储蓄目标，2026年为79,000元。
terminology.ms: Jumlah Penjagaan Kesihatan Asas: sasaran MediSave untuk kesihatan di hari tua; $79,000 pada 2026.
terminology.ta: அடிப்படை சுகாதார தொகை: முதுமையில் சுகாதாரத்துக்கான மெடிசேவ் இலக்கு; 2026-ல் $79,000.

terminology.plainEnglish: The interest your CPF savings would have earned; must be refunded when you sell a home bought with CPF.
terminology.zh: 应计利息：你的公积金储蓄本应赚取的利息；用公积金买的房子卖出时须连本带息退回。
terminology.ms: Faedah Terakru: faedah yang sepatutnya diperoleh simpanan CPF; mesti dipulangkan apabila menjual rumah.
terminology.ta: சேர்ந்த வட்டி: உங்கள் CPF சேமிப்பு ஈட்டியிருக்கும் வட்டி; வீட்டை விற்கும்போது திரும்பச் செலுத்த வேண்டும்.

terminology.plainEnglish: Choosing who receives your CPF savings after you pass away, and how much.
terminology.zh: 公积金提名：选择你身故后谁能领取你的公积金存款及金额。
terminology.ms: Penamaan CPF: memilih siapa menerima simpanan CPF anda selepas anda meninggal.
terminology.ta: CPF நியமனம்: நீங்கள் இறந்த பிறகு உங்கள் CPF சேமிப்பை யார் பெறுவது என்பதைத் தேர்வு செய்தல்.

terminology.plainEnglish: Basic lifelong health insurance for large hospital bills and costly treatments.
terminology.zh: 终身健保：用于大额住院和昂贵治疗的基本终身健康保险。
terminology.ms: MediShield Life: insurans kesihatan asas seumur hidup untuk bil hospital besar.
terminology.ta: மெடிஷீல்டு லைஃப்: பெரிய மருத்துவமனை செலவுகளுக்கான அடிப்படை வாழ்நாள் காப்பீடு.

terminology.plainEnglish: Long-term care insurance giving monthly cash payouts if you become severely disabled.
terminology.zh: 终身护保：若严重失能可获每月现金入息的长期护理保险。
terminology.ms: CareShield Life: insurans penjagaan jangka panjang dengan pencen bulanan jika hilang upaya teruk.
terminology.ta: கேர்ஷீல்டு லைஃப்: கடுமையான இயலாமை ஏற்பட்டால் மாதாந்திர பணம் வழங்கும் நீண்டகால காப்பீடு.

terminology.plainEnglish: The age your CPF monthly payouts can start — currently 65.
terminology.zh: 入息领取年龄：可开始领取每月公积金入息的年龄，目前为65岁。
terminology.ms: Umur Kelayakan Pencen: umur pencen bulanan CPF boleh bermula — kini 65 tahun.
terminology.ta: கொடுப்பனவு தகுதி வயது: CPF மாதாந்திர கொடுப்பனவு தொடங்கும் வயது — தற்போது 65.

terminology.plainEnglish: The share of your wages that you and your employer put into CPF each month.
terminology.zh: 缴交率：你和雇主每月存入公积金的工资比例。
terminology.ms: Kadar Caruman: bahagian gaji yang anda dan majikan masukkan ke CPF setiap bulan.
terminology.ta: பங்களிப்பு விகிதம்: ஒவ்வொரு மாதமும் நீங்களும் முதலாளரும் CPF-ல் சேர்க்கும் ஊதியப் பங்கு.

terminology.plainEnglish: The monthly wage limit above which CPF contributions are not required; $8,000 from 2026.
terminology.zh: 公积金薪金顶限：超过此每月薪金不需缴交公积金；2026年起为8,000元。
terminology.ms: Siling Gaji CPF: had gaji bulanan di mana caruman CPF tidak diperlukan; $8,000 dari 2026.
terminology.ta: CPF சம்பள உச்சவரம்பு: இதற்கு மேல் CPF பங்களிப்பு தேவையில்லை; 2026 முதல் $8,000.

terminology.plainEnglish: Voluntarily adding cash to your or a loved one's retirement savings, possibly for tax relief.
terminology.zh: 退休存款填补计划：自愿为自己或亲人增加退休存款，或可享税务减免。
terminology.ms: Penambahan Jumlah Persaraan: menambah tunai ke simpanan persaraan secara sukarela.
terminology.ta: ஓய்வூதிய தொகை நிரப்புதல்: உங்கள் அல்லது அன்புக்குரியவரின் ஓய்வூதிய சேமிப்பை தானாக அதிகரித்தல்.

terminology.plainEnglish: Mortgage insurance that pays off your HDB loan if you die or become permanently disabled.
terminology.zh: 房屋保障计划：若身故或永久失能，可偿还你的组屋贷款的房贷保险。
terminology.ms: Skim Perlindungan Rumah: insurans yang melangsaikan pinjaman HDB jika anda meninggal atau hilang upaya.
terminology.ta: வீட்டு பாதுகாப்பு திட்டம்: இறப்பு அல்லது நிரந்தர இயலாமையின்போது HDB கடனை அடைக்கும் காப்பீடு.

terminology.plainEnglish: Extra quarterly cash for eligible seniors who earned less during their working years.
terminology.zh: 乐龄补贴计划：为工作期间收入较低的合格年长者提供额外季度现金。
terminology.ms: Skim Sokongan Silver: tunai suku tahunan tambahan untuk warga emas berpendapatan rendah.
terminology.ta: சில்வர் சப்போர்ட் திட்டம்: குறைந்த வருமானம் ஈட்டிய தகுதியான முதியோருக்கு கூடுதல் காலாண்டு பணம்.

terminology.plainEnglish: Singapore's trusted digital login used to access CPF and other government services online.
terminology.zh: Singpass：新加坡可信的数码登录，用于在线访问公积金等政府服务。
terminology.ms: Singpass: log masuk digital dipercayai Singapura untuk akses CPF dan perkhidmatan kerajaan.
terminology.ta: Singpass: CPF மற்றும் அரசு சேவைகளை அணுக சிங்கப்பூரின் நம்பகமான டிஜிட்டல் உள்நுழைவு.
